content:
matt: heads up — seeing p95 east-west latency spikes on batchers in us-west-2 around 00:30-01:00, correlates with nightly prefix caching job
julia: how big are the spikes?
matt: p95 jumps from ~8ms to 120-200ms for inter-gpu RPCs, token throughput drops, some jobs hit retry backoff
kiran: any packet loss? rdma errors in dmesg?
matt: yes saw mlx5_core: error: LINK_DOWN / port flaps, and RDMA CM retransmits. tcpdump shows sporadic retransmits. attaching snippet
matt: ```
17:01:32.123456 IP 10.0.12.5.4321 > 10.0.12.7.5432: Flags [P.], seq 1:145, ack 1, win 342, length 144
17:01:32.126789 IP 10.0.12.5.4321 > 10.0.12.7.5432: Flags [.], ack 1, win 342, length 0
17:01:32.223456 IP 10.0.12.5.4321 > 10.0.12.7.5432: Flags [P.], seq 145:289, ack 1, win 342, length 144
```
julia: could be NIC offload issue during burst. any ethtool output around the time?
matt: ethtool -k shows GRO/GSO on, but we saw large GRO coalesces spike. tried ethtool -K to disable GRO on one node, latencies normalized in canary
kiran: did you see MTU mismatch? sometimes tor config pushes jumbo to 9000 then host falls back
matt: MTU consistent at 9000 across rack. but one switch port reported smaller mtu in logs during the window (maybe control-plane push).
infra-oncall: deploy bot: rolled a kpatch 2.6.32-rc that changed mlx firmware last night at 00:10 UTC. could be correlated
tara: any relation to batching window config? batching -> higher packet rates -> more coalescing -> driver bug
matt: yes spikes only when batch size > 64 tokens per request and concurrent requests > 200
julia: run iperf3 between two affected nodes during window? also check rdma pingpong (rping)
matt: ran iperf3 — throughput steady, but latency p95 had microbursts. rdma pingpong saw increased retries in CM: 'RNR NAK' events
kiran: plan: 1) throttle batch ramp (workaround) 2) disable GRO/GSO on host for affected nodes 3) coordinate with infra to rollback mlx firmware if confirmed 4) add RDMA error alerts
matt: also need to add fallback policy in router to send to dedicated region (us-west-1) if p95 > 100ms for >30s
tara: cost impact? shifting region during peak will add cross-region egress and double token cost for those packets
matt: rough calc: moving 10% traffic for 1h costs ~$120 extra for egress + CPU bill. but avoids throttled jobs and missed SLAs
julia: creating postmortem ticket and a small runbook for oncall to flip GRO and roll back firmware
matt: oncall action items: tag affected nodes, hold new deployments to mlx driver, enable temporary batch-slowdown flag
infra-oncall:ACK — will open infra incident (INC-21245) and notify networking vendor
matt: thanks. i'll attach logs and exact node list to the incident.
raj: +1. reassigning to kiran for driver rollback testing
deploy-bot: incident INC-21245 created by infra-oncall
